likely_semantic_meaning: first timestamp where Cloudflare detector observed hijack evidence
evidence/notes: Represents first hijack evidence in raw hijack schema.

likely_semantic_meaning: last timestamp where Cloudflare detector observed hijack evidence
evidence/notes: Used instead of max_msg_ts by design.

likely_semantic_meaning: last detector message timestamp; may include unrelated/non-hijack detector persistence
evidence/notes: Must not be used as hijack end time.
Normalized duration is calculated from max_hijack_ts - min_hijack_ts.
Usually close to min_ts but not necessarily full event start.

likely_semantic_meaning: first observation associated with the leak detector event
evidence/notes: Best available leak start in Cloudflare route-leak schema.

likely_semantic_meaning: last observation associated with the detector event; may not prove continuous leaking for the whole interval
evidence/notes: Long leak intervals should be reviewed before defining feature windows.
Does not by itself define the start/end timestamps.
Cloudflare outage records are explicit reported event intervals.
Long outages may need reviewed collection windows but should not be auto-changed.

likely_semantic_meaning: reported or normalized outage interval length
evidence/notes: Checked against startDate/endDate during partition audit.
Useful for review but not a timestamp.
